title: Parity of the Composite Trigonometric Function f(x) = sin(x^2)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Determine whether the function f(x) = sin(x^2) is even, odd, or neither, and give reasons for your answer.

steps.title: Substitute -x into the Function
steps.explanation: Replace x with -x inside the squared argument of the sine function.
steps.why: The exponent 2 applies to the input x before the sine function is evaluated.

steps.title: Simplify the Squared Argument
steps.explanation: Because (-x)^2 = x^2 for all real x, the argument of the sine function is unchanged, giving sin((-x)^2) = sin(x^2) = f(x).
steps.why: Squaring absorbs the negative sign before the outer function sin(u) is applied.

steps.title: Conclude Function Parity
steps.explanation: Since f(-x) = f(x) for all real numbers x, f(x) = sin(x^2) is an even function.
steps.why: Any function of the form g(x^2) is even because its inner argument x^2 is even.
